newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission to open intervention stores for heavy steers.
newsitem.headline: Commission to open intervention stores for heavy steers.

text.p: The European Commission will open a special programme allowing steers over the weight limit to be bought into intervention stores during September, a European Union official said on Thursday.
"The amendment to the regulation was approved by the European Union's sugar management committee on Wednesday and has still to be formally adopted by the Commission," the official said.

Farmers, who were unable to sell steers on the open market because of mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), will now be able to sell animals over the 390 kilogram weight into intervention stores at the 390 kg price limit.
The measure will mainly benefit Irish farmers who have been badly hit by the collapse in their export markets due to BSE.

"Many farmers have had to hold back steers and they now exceed the weight limit. This measure which is only for the month of September will allow them to sell into intervention although they will only be paid for 390 kilograms whatever the weight of their animals," the official said.
When the Commission opened intervention because of the BSE crisis in May it allowed a temporary derogation increasing the normal weight limit of 340 kg to 400 kg.
"This was on a reducing basis and the limit now stands at 390 kilograms," the official added. REUTER
